remaining_findings.title: Reject or gap a named single-child receipt reused with a different child-kind contract
remaining_findings.consequence: The named receipt guard compares only decision_id/operation/parents/basis. A persisted term child and a new rule child share that same key; the kind/scope filter removes the old child from candidate matching, then the empty list triggers a new allocation. The same named one-child decision consequently describes two different typed child allocations without explicit contract-change diagnosis. Original content correction/rename is repaired, but the required exact child-contract and changed/colliding-decision boundary remains incomplete.
remaining_findings.reproducer: Merge North/South terms into one Together term with decision_id merge-child-contract. Replay that ID, operation, parent IDs and basis while changing the child collection/kind to rules with R-Together. Only the origin child locator changes from /terms/0 to /rules/0. The implementation assigns a new rule ID instead of rejecting or preserving an unresolved contract conflict.
remaining_findings.observed: The assertion forbidding a silently assigned replacement child fails; no explicit receipt-contract conflict is returned.
remaining_findings.expected_result_justification: R04's required change pins the persisted receipt/decision and exact child contract, while its verification requires changed/colliding decision rejection. Logical kind is already an explicit discriminator in the persisted registry. A named one-child receipt must not silently acquire a different typed output contract merely because matching filtered the old output away; a changed contract needs explicit rejection/gap or a separately identified decision.
remaining_findings.required_change: Compare the persisted named child contract before filtering out existing receipt children and allocating replacements. Preserve the logical-kind/scope/persistent-key contract independent of locators and content. Reject incompatible reuse or retain an explicit contract conflict; use a new decision identifier for a deliberately different output contract. Preserve valid text correction/rename and keyed ambiguity handling.
